scope: Source-only review of exact Verilatorv5.052 as an alternative existing HDL backend. No acquired code executed, no build or catalogue reclassification.

tag_identity.proof: Pinned GitHub ref/tag API records agree; this is not a verified signed-tag claim.

licenses.project_declaration: LGPL-3.0-only OR Artistic-2.0, per original README and per-source SPDX headers. Test Verilog files declare CC0-1.0 where stated. No package-wide legal audit claimed.

findings.finding: The documented option is experimental/developer-only. This release emits a FUTURE warning that it is unsupported and rejects hierarchical use. The ordinary generation pipeline still unconditionally invokes unknown conversion, replacing X/Z constants with configured known/random values. The few option-dependent expression branches are incomplete wildcard-operator stubs, not full four-state execution.
findings.required: Do not suppress the warning and label a selected run four-state. A different implemented backend or separately evidenced existing-backend development is required.

findings.finding: The array assignment test uses known8-bit constants only and does not enable --fourstate. It checks declared type compatibility, not retention of X/Z in RAM. The explicit --fourstate regression expects failure. The archive has12 files with t_fourstate in their path.
findings.required: Selected RAM unknown/reset observations remain mandatory; ordinary array support is insufficient.

findings.finding: Scalar/vector VPI reads write bval=0; writes consume aval only. Array vector reads also zero bval, and array writes explicitly ignore the fourState argument. The current simulator transport requires raw X/Z values, which this interface cannot preserve unchanged.

The documented implementation converts supported tristate structures to two-state input/output/enable signals and requires external resolution for external drivers. It does not establish the current resolved-X/Z inout contract.

Future relative RW/RO callbacks can be registered. The generated main evaluates once, polls value-change callbacks, then calls RW and immediately RO without re-evaluating changed HDL. The source therefore does not establish settled RO after a drive. Value-change polling after eval also does not prove every same-time delta transition is retained.
findings.inference: Our current exact NBA/X/Z sequence and clock-boundary tests cannot be assumed to pass from callback names alone. A custom harness could address scheduling, but does not supply missing four-state storage.

decision: Do not spend a selected-model build on unchanged5.052 for the required four-state contract. Keep it as an explicitly limited candidate; pursue the compiled CVC path and its separately reviewed scheduler adaptation/equivalence tests. This is not evidence that any S9 hardware or firmware target is incompatible.
required_equivalence_gates: two510-case RAM suites including unknown/parity/reset behavior
raw X/Z event order and time-zero NBA settling
same-edge input/clock ordering and split/unsplit equality
bounded failure/cancellation and honest measured throughput
